title: Luang Prabang Half Marathon 2026 Review: What the 2025 Run for Children Was Like
seo_title: Luang Prabang Half Marathon 2026 Review | Run for Children
meta_description: Luang Prabang Half Marathon review: 3,000+ runners through the UNESCO town on 25 October 2025, past temples on the Mekong, raising funds for a children's hospital.
dek: The Run for Children in Luang Prabang is a charity half marathon through a UNESCO World Heritage town. Here is what the October 2025 edition was like, ahead of 2026.
verdict: The Luang Prabang Half Marathon is a charity race in a remarkable setting. The 2025 edition, on Saturday 25 October, drew more than 3,000 participants [1]. It started at the National Museum, the former Royal Palace, and passed temples along the Mekong and Nam Khan rivers, with the morning alms procession under way outside the palace during the race [1]. It raises money for the Lao Friends Hospital for Children, which gives free care to more than 35,000 children a year [1]. If you want a race where the town and the cause matter more than the clock, this is a lovely one.

sections.heading: The 2025 Edition
paragraphs: The race was held on Saturday 25 October 2025 and attracted more than 3,000 participants [1]. It began at the National Museum, the former Royal Palace, in the old town [1].

The route passed temples along the Mekong and Nam Khan rivers, letting runners take in Luang Prabang's mix of cultural and natural heritage [1]. The monks' morning alms ceremony took place outside the Royal Palace during the race [1].

sections.heading: A Race for a Hospital
paragraphs: The event is organised by the Lao Friends Hospital for Children, with partners, to raise money and awareness for the hospital [1]. It is the only paediatric hospital in northern Laos giving free medical care, to more than 35,000 children each year [1].
That shapes the event. This is a community fundraiser in a heritage town, not a race built for fast times.

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a destination race with meaning. Running through Luang Prabang at dawn, past its temples and the alms procession, is the reason to go, and the entry fee supports a free children's hospital.
Be respectful on the course. The race shares the old town's streets with a living religious tradition at dawn, so give the alms procession space.
This review is compiled from published reporting on the 2025 edition. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.
